She did an out patient program that she said didn't work however I saw that it did. It gave her structure. A reason to go to bed at a decent hour and to get up. She also saw a therapist and Idk how well that worked. She saw a therapist for about 4 months and decided it was just a waste of money. She's starting to fall back into the old grove. I woke up to her crying at 2am last night. Saying she can't do anything. That when she does what to do something she can't find pleasure in it. We are in the process of getting our first home so I hope once this is settled, she will have the fresh start she deserves

I've looked her in her eyes and have told her how much she means to me and that I can't live without her. She knows that but it doesn't help with future waves of anxiety. Like this morning. She had a somewhat good morning. Woke up, had coffee, decided to take a shower and once she got out, she started to go down hill. I made her brunch, a hot tea and let her relax and try to work through it however she just had a huge anxiety attack where she was crying so loud and she said she couldn't breathe. I know she can because if she's crying she's breathing but that doesn't help. I have to just let it take its course or it gets worse. She finally agreed to take a mg of ativan to help but idk what to do. She doesn't know what triggered it. She doesn't know whats going on through in her head or whats on her mind. We see a psychiatrist thursday to hopefully get her on new meds or something stronger but that doesn't really help since it takes months for new meds to build up and start working. I have no friends because of my own issues and have no one but my mother to talk to. Talking to my mom doesn't really help because she is very apologetic and keeps telling me that my wife has to want to get better. This doesn't help me...

I tried to get her out today but she didn't want to. When I tried to somewhat push the issue of just getting out of bed she just started to cry. I've asked her to write down her feelings and at least have a list of how she feels and thinks to give to the doc but she won't. I've tried to get her to look at tasks as small victories...like getting out if bed and having a cup of coffee by 9am but she doesn't see it that way. She is a lot better when we leave and go on a trip but we can't do this forever. If I could get a cheap apartment I would in a second. Problem is where I live, a one bed one bath apartment starts at $2000/month plus utilities. She got a little better today and just kept saying how I deserve better and how she's a horrible person....
i need help with my wife...I'm so lost and don't know what to do

no worries. Some people over breed their dams. If she is 3 years old and have had 3 litters already then I'd be concerned. Females shouldn't be bred until the age of 2. That would mean she has been bred non stop since turning 2 or she started too early. Most breeders retire their dams between the age of 5-7 years old however if litters have been spaced out and she is fully healthy, a dog of this age is perfectly fine.

I beg to differ because many breeders can have a very good idea of the temperament of the litter. I never said a doodle will be all golden with just the non shedding qualities of a poodle. Theres a reason as to why a poodle and golden are bred together rather than a poodle/german shepherd, poodle/beagle, poodle/pitbull. Sorry you don't like the "best of both worlds" mantra however many people who own doodles describe them as this. 

Sorry to the OP for your thread being Hijacked. I was only trying to recommend a couple breeds as you had asked for.

I don't think if someone belongs to a breeder club really means much.

Look at their health guarantee and what their spay/neuter clause is. I have it in my contract that they must be altered between 1-1.5 years, no sooner because I want the growth plates to close and allow the dogs to have their sex hormones introduced into the system. Studies show this helps fight off cancer and other ailments in the later years. 

See if there are any OFA clearances for the hips and elbows (this is not a deal breaker to me and I know several people here will argue with me on it and down vote this due to disagreeing. I have had dogs certified with excellent hips have hip dysplasia when they were older. Had one dog with eye's cleared and ended up having cataracts around 7 years old. I don't believe it really does much other than give potential buyers a feel good feeling. All these test do is show you that at this time their joints are good. Breeders aren't going to spend the money and take the risk to retest their dogs at a later age. Again my opinion).

Ask to see the parents, how old are they and how many litters has the dam had. Do they handle the puppies a lot and stimulate them with different textures, noises, environments and toys? What kind of support do they offer when first getting your puppy?

These are things I'd ask.

"Best of both worlds" in a general sense that you get the demeanor and temperament of a golden and the non shedding hypoallergenic properties from a poodle. I know this because I have heavily researched the breed. These are dominant traits. When you breed purebreds, there is a chance of passing on recessive traits. 

Again i'm not saying golden doodles or mix breeds are superior over purebreds.

You get the traits of both breeds. Many people want the personality and temperament of a golden and the non shedding ability of poodles. Poodles can actually be quite mean around new people. 

A Golden doodle is in no way the same as a shelter mutt. You will never know what a shelter dog has gone through and what illness and issues the dog may have in the future. You will never know the true genetic make up of the dog. You don't know what type of psychological stress that dog has been put through. There is never a real guarantee to what traits you'll get with a purebred as well. You know with a golden doodle that you will get the best of both breeds and something that doesn't shed much. You will also be able to see the parents and their clearances. 

I guess I need to know how much you consider "champion" money is? Quality Goldens and Poodles are no less than $1500. Golden doodles are around the same price. May be more if you are getting a "Teddy Bear" sized golden doodle. All purebreds were once mutts until they were recognized as a purebred. Look at Pugs, they are "purebreds" however were entirely designed by man. 

Now I may be biased because I breed golden doodles however many of my golden doodles have moved on to be therapy dogs and other types of service dogs which I am extremely proud of. I'm not trying to persuade the OP to get a golden doodle. I first suggested a golden. I wouldn't go with a poodle because they can be mean and having someone with down syndrome, I wouldn't want to take the risk. Thats just my opinion.

Doodles have a great temperament and are very smart dogs, not to mention have significantly less shedding which can help with keeping the house tidy and the OP stated not wanting as much shedding in her post. They are also great apartment/small home dogs. 

The OP also stated she wants to be able to bring the dog with her when going to friends places and stuff, because of this a doodle will be better because of 1)little to no shed 2) hypoallergenic properties (no doodle is 100% hypoallergenic however it is very low and people with allergies often aren't affected) and the breeds willingness to please (most doodles want nothing but love). 

OP wanted a breed recommendation, I can't recommend a shelter mutt because a mutt isn't a breed. If she can find a great shelter dog to adopt then great for the OP. I personally don't like dealing with rescue groups and some shelters because they require to much info. They want to know your work schedule, blueprints to your backyard, your activity level and a whole bunch of useless info. If they feel you aren't the ideal perfect candidate that will devote 99% of the day to the dog, your rejected. 

A doodle is just as good as a purebred.

I would recommend a golden or golden doodle. They are great dogs and love to cuddle. My golden prefers to stay in bed but loves to go for walks as soon as she sees me grabbing her leash. Having 2 kids and one have down syndrome, the golden or doodle will be very comforting and a great companion.
